tips: Add Suica to your Apple/Google Wallet while waiting at the MSP gate — you'll breeze past the ticket machines at Haneda.
Fill out Visit Japan Web now and screenshot the QRs; airplane Wi-Fi is unreliable and immigration requires them.
Hit the ATM at Haneda or a 7-Eleven in Shinjuku; with the USD/JPY rate at ~161.5, your dollars stretch far for cash-first spots.
If Ichiran's line is brutal, pivot one stop north to Shin-Okubo Koreatown for KFC (Korean fried chicken) and cheese dogs.
Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast — book ASAP if not already locked in, otherwise Mag's Park or Hikarie Sky Lobby are great free backups.
Blue Cave illumination draws dense crowds after 18:00; go early or accept the shuffle.
Senso-ji at 08:30 is the move — by 10:00 the main hall and Nakamise are packed.
If the Skytree queue is insane, pivot to the Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view with a drink in hand.
teamLab Planets is already booked (nice!), but if anyone gets sick, Borderless at Azabudai Hills is the sister exhibit to check.
Golden Gai bars seat 4-6 max; split into pairs and rotate meeting spots rather than trying to squeeze 8 into a stall.
December is peak clarity for Fuji — if the sky is cloudless, the Enoshima Sea Candle view at 16:32 is your best shot.
The Enoden coastal tram gets crowded; try to board at the first stop (Kamakura Station) to secure seats for the scenic run.
Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
Pack FIRST before Golden Gai tonight — bags must close and the shinkansen waits for no one tomorrow morning.
Sit on the LEFT side (seats E) on the Nozomi shinkansen for the Fuji view around minute 40 out of Tokyo.
Pontocho dinner for 8 is locked; have two scouts arrive early to hold the riverside seating.
Fushimi Inari at 06:45 is the golden ticket — past Yotsutsuji the crowds vanish for the summit loop.
Funaoka Onsen's electric bath is wild; brace yourself and don't stay in more than a few seconds on the first zap.
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at 07:15 beats the buses; if you want it empty, 06:30 is even better.
Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter (since Dec 13) — skip the climb and stick to the deer and temples.
Pre-order your KFC Christmas Bucket NOW if you haven't — Japanese outlets sell out weeks in advance for the Dec 24 tradition.
Rikuro's jiggly cheesecake near Namba is a must-buy; grab two for the house before they sell out tonight.
Rope-drop USJ 45 minutes early to hit Super Nintendo World first; Express Passes are a lifesaver but the early sprint seals it.
If Mario Kart lines are brutal, use the single-rider line to cut 60% off the wait time.
Hiroshima is the longest day of the trip — if anyone is redlining, skip Miyajima, do the museum unhurried, and meet at the station.
Okonomimura is fun, but Nagata-ya near the Dome is the locals' pick; split the squad and debate on the ferry.
Midosuji Illumination covers 4km of lit boulevard — walk south from Umeda to maximize the glow.
551 Horai pork buns sell out nightly; grab a 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner to secure house breakfast.
Sit on the LEFT side (seats A) on the shinkansen to Himeji for a clear view of Mt. Fuji on the way out.
Tonight is the night to organize all tax-free receipts and check that purchases are accessible — customs CAN ask on exit.
Overslept? Nozomi runs every ~10 min until noon; an 11:00 departure still makes Haneda by 14:15, so breathe.
Zero out your Suica balance at the konbini or vending machines before flying; refunds at the station take time.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.5, your dollars go far — withdraw cash at 7-Eleven or Post Office ATMs for the best exchange rates and avoid airport currency counters.
For tax-free shopping, keep all receipts stapled in your passport and purchases accessible in your luggage — Japanese customs can and does check on exit, and disorganized bags cause delays.
Winter days are short (sunset ~16:30); plan outdoor sightseeing and illumination walks for the afternoon, and keep indoor backups (museums, arcades, depachika) ready for the early dark.
